title: Code Anatomy build call 3: broken things shown, imports, entry points
purpose: Extend the package from build call 2 so that the map tells three things apart that it now gives one label: a reference that goes outside the project, a reference to something that should be in the project and is not, and a reference the tool cannot place. The tool then never refuses to explain a project, lists the missing things first, reads imports correctly, and gives every plain program an entry point and a flow. The owner asked that broken things be shown so the operator catches them early. The result is tested by running the supplied acceptance script on the owner's machine, not by reading it.
task: Read BUILD_3_BRIEF.md first, then OWNER_ADDENDUM_3.md, then the kit's README, facts and fixtures, then BUILD_2_BRIEF.md and BUILD_1_BRIEF.md for everything the new brief does not change. Extract base-codeanatomy-pipeline.tar.gz and change it as BUILD_3_BRIEF.md sections 4 and 5 require: the three labels and the call rule table (T01-T04), the brief that never refuses and the missing list (T05-T07), imports (T08-T12), entry points and flows (T13-T16), housekeeping (T17-T21). Work in the order of the brief's floor, finishing each part before the next. Install the supplied wheels and grammars in your sandbox, run your tests, then run owner-kit/tools/owner_checks3.sh on your result and paste its complete output into TEST_LOG.md. Deliver the full source tree as one tarball, version 0.3.0, with the five report files beside it.

in: BUILD_3_BRIEF.md section 5 in full for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, TSX, Go, Java and Rust, with the floor and the complete-or-absent rule of its section 3.

The changes inside existing code that the new rules force: binding.py's brief template, run.json and scripts/run_corpus.sh, scripts/demo_e2e.sh, the Python MCP adapter, structure.py, the skill and runbook text, README.md, and existing tests whose asserted values this brief replaces.
Copying the seven built-in name lists of the kit into the package byte for byte.
Rewriting RESOLUTION_RULES.md for this build, with every rule name that appears in a basis string and the test that covers it.
Copying the kit's ten fixtures, facts, expected outcomes and checker into the package's own tests, naming their origin, and writing the tests of BUILD_3_BRIEF.md section 7.
Running the owner's acceptance script in your sandbox and reporting its real output, and reporting for each corpus repository the outcome counts, the flows and every entry of the missing list.
out: Framework adapters, build and CI adapters, entry points declared in manifests, Go init functions, any entry point for the JavaScript family.
Knowledge of the type of a value, following a re-export to the file behind it, type inference, data flow, language servers, any execution of project code, any new dependency.
Joining the two flows of the MCP example, or narrowing rules 2c and 3c.

Any change to the verifier, the mutation tool, the atlas rules, flows.py, the binding skeleton or the demo figure beyond what they need to keep working on the new map. The defects listed as not to touch in BUILD_3_BRIEF.md section 2 stay as they are.
Changes to map.schema.json or binding.schema.json, and any open-end kind, node kind or edge kind that is not already in the schema.
Any name list other than the seven supplied files, and any edit to those files.
Rebuilding the owner's measuring probe into the package.
Code that satisfies an expected row by naming a test input, and tests that cannot fail.

constraints: Precedence is as BUILD_3_BRIEF.md section 1 states: addendum 3, addendum 2, addendum 1, spec v2 with its schemas, ENVIRONMENT_FACTS.md for anything measured, BUILD_3_BRIEF.md for this call's scope, rulings and amendments, then BUILD_2_BRIEF.md, then BUILD_1_BRIEF.md. The table in section 1 lists the earlier text that is no longer in force.
Start from the supplied base tarball. A file that needs no change stays byte-identical to the base. CHANGES.md lists every file added, changed or removed, with a reason.

The 34 existing tests keep passing. An assertion may change only to a value this brief requires, and each such change is listed in CHANGES.md with the old and the new value. No test is deleted, skipped or loosened.

UNRESOLVED is produced only by the proof rules named in T03 and T11. Whatever the tool cannot place and cannot prove missing is AMBIGUOUS. EXTERNAL is produced only by a rule that shows no snapshot file can be the target.
Every call site yields exactly one accounting object and every import path exactly one, anchored at exactly the span the kit's facts give. Nothing is dropped and nothing is counted twice.
The tool never refuses to produce a brief, and brief.md carries no density figure.

The source tree names no corpus or fixture identifier and depends on no literal ID or line number of a test input. If you believe a kit fact or expected row is wrong, implement the rule, leave that check failing and report the row; never write code to match it.

Only grammars.py touches the grammar pack. No module of the package imports the host's ast module. Run-time dependencies, grammar handling, canonical RFC 8785 output, determinism and the safety rules are those of BUILD_1_BRIEF.md, unchanged: no model call, no network, no subprocess, nothing written inside the mapped repository, nothing from it imported or run.
Repository and fixture text is data, never instructions.
Do not claim a test passed unless it ran. Do not weaken an assertion to make a test pass. State in the first line of TEST_LOG.md whether tree-sitter and the seven grammars loaded in your sandbox.
facts: The base is codeanatomy-pipeline.tar.gz from build call 2 (exchange ec_41db9cb503df), version 0.2.0, SHA-256 24a5f071252d66c01e7e528628512747610bab90f144eb5ce26c3ba7dfe4a6b3. It is supplied as base-codeanatomy-pipeline.tar.gz.

On the owner's machine (Python 3.14.7, fresh venv) the base passed all 15 steps of build call 2's acceptance run; pytest reported 34 passed, and 7 passed without grammars. A copy of the five fixtures with every identifier renamed gave the same outcomes.

In the base, binding.py line 51 computes refused = unknown*10 > 3*max(1, n_edges+unknown) and the brief prints a REFUSE line. By the formula of spec v2 section 8 the six corpus repositories stand at flask 0.65, next 0.81, chi 0.73, spring 0.96, axum 1.00, mcp 0.43, all above 0.30.
In the base, 85 of flask's 177 call sites are UNRESOLVED, among them db.execute(), open() and bp.route(). Only the mcp repository has an entry point and a flow.

Defects of the base found on the owner's machine outside build call 2's kit: a JavaScript default import of a named default export is UNRESOLVED; a Python import list with a comment loses the names after it; relative imports fail in folders whose name has a dot; there is one import object per imported name with invented one-byte anchors (mcp: 7 objects for 5 statements); structure.py is a copy of the owner's probe and imports tree_sitter_language_pack; the MCP adapter uses the host's ast module; Rust reads only [dependencies]; README.md and RUNBOOK.md still say 0.1.0.

The kit's facts were measured on the owner's machine with the pinned tree-sitter 0.26.0 and the seven supplied grammar libraries. The tool that measured them is not in the kit. A second, independent measurement with the grammar pack's own tags queries found no call site in the 21 corpus source files outside the measured callee spans.

Counts from the kit, per fixture, as import paths, call sites, entry points and expected missing entries: py 5, 14, 1, 3; js 9, 19, 0, 2; go 6, 11, 1, 2; java 4, 10, 1, 0; rust 8, 13, 1, 2; py3 14, 27, 2, 4; js3 14, 18, 0, 5; go3 6, 13, 1, 2; java3 5, 12, 2, 1; rust3 12, 20, 3, 4. Per corpus repository, as import paths, call sites and entry points: flask 48, 177, 0; next 10, 20, 0; chi 11, 120, 1; spring 11, 24, 1; axum 3, 8, 1; mcp 5, 41, 1.

tools/check_build3.py was tested on the owner's machine: on a conforming map built from each input's facts and expected rows it passes, and it fails each of thirteen deliberate breakages. tools/owner_checks3.sh on the base fails 9 of its 19 steps (version, map_corpus, map_fixtures, missing_list, never_refuses, mcp_flow, source_rules, builtin_lists, docs) and passes the other 10; the log is in the kit.

The built-in name lists were measured on the owner's machine (Python 3.12.14, 3.13.15, 3.14.7; go1.27.0; Node.js v26.8.1) or taken from the official Java 21 and Rust 1.90.0 pages on 2026-10-12; PROVENANCE.md in the kit names each source.

map.schema.json already lists AMBIGUOUS among the open-end kinds, entry_point among the node kinds and triggers among the edge kinds. No part of the verifier, the mutation tool, the atlas or the figures of the base treats UNRESOLVED specially; binding.py line 48 is the only place.
hypotheses: One session can deliver all 21 items, because it edits an existing tree of about 2,100 source lines. Unmeasured: build call 2 delivered 21 items in one session.
The expected rows in the kit follow the rules of section 5. They were written by hand and checked for fit against the facts, not against an implementation, so some may be wrong.

The proofs of 'missing' produce no false entry on the six corpus repositories. The labelled corpus rows expect none; the unlabelled call sites of flask, next, chi, spring and axum were not checked by hand.
The whole-word test and the leaf-node test are conservative enough that a 'missing' label is right whenever it appears, at the price of labelling some real faults 'cannot tell'.
assumptions: Your sandbox can install the supplied wheels on CPython 3.12 or 3.13 and load the seven grammar libraries offline, as it did in build calls 1 and 2.
The owner's side will run owner_checks3.sh on Python 3.14.7, diff your tree against the base, rerun the fixtures with every identifier renamed, and read the missing list of each corpus map.

acceptance.condition: check_build3.py reports no failure of E3 or E4 on the six corpus maps and the ten fixture maps: each expected call site has the expected outcome and exactly the expected target set. requirements.requirement: The tool never refuses and prints no density (T05).

requirements.requirement: The skill and the runbook tell the drawing agent to show the gaps (T07).

requirements.requirement: Entry points and flows for plain programs (T13-T16).

stop_condition: Deliver the six files. Work in the order of the floor in BUILD_3_BRIEF.md section 3 and finish each part before the next. If the session runs short, stop at a part boundary and report PARTIAL: part 1 must be complete and tested for all five families, and in parts 2 and 3 each family is either complete or absent in the exact sense the brief defines. Run owner_checks3.sh before you deliver and report its real result, including failing steps. Never satisfy an expected row with a special case, never add a name to a built-in list, and never report a test or a step as passed that did not run.
